rule: "design-system" is 13 characters (ODD) -> reference = A.png, ours = B.png

A.what: Pleco iOS headword/detail screen for 几乎 jīhū (HSK 3): headword, level badge, pinyin + Jyutping rows, DICT/CHARS/WORDS/SENTS tabs, POS, gloss, four example sentences each set hanzi + bold pinyin + English.

B.what: hskquiz /quiz/1 teaching card at 375x812 (2x), light theme: NEW WORD eyebrow, 这些 at ~130px, tone-coloured pinyin zhè xiē, gloss, POS, pinned Got it button.

why_this_pair: The design-system piece is judged on type scale, spacing rhythm and how Chinese is set. Pleco's entry screen is the densest test of a Chinese type scale in the reference folder — seven distinct type roles on one screen — and our quiz prompt is the screen a learner spends the most time on. Both are single-headword screens built around one large hanzi with tone-marked pinyin beneath it.
caveat_for_the_record: A is a dictionary entry and B is a flashcard, so B carrying less content is partly by design. The question put to the judge is about the visual system, not feature parity.
